# Lamentations 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** How the-gold has-become-dim, the-fine gold changed! The-stones-of [the]-sanctuary are-poured-out at-the-head-of every street.

**2** The-precious sons-of Zion, weighed-against fine-gold — how they-are-reckoned as-earthen-pots, the-work-of [the]-hands-of a-potter!

**3** Even jackals draw-out the-breast; they-nurse their-young; the-daughter-of my-people has-become cruel, like-ostriches in-the-wilderness.

**4** The-tongue-of the-nursing-child cleaves to-his-palate from-thirst; young-children ask-for bread — no-one breaks-[it] for-them.

**5** Those-who-ate delicacies are-desolate in-the-streets; those-raised on-crimson embrace ash-heaps.

**6** And-the-iniquity-of the-daughter-of my-people was-greater than-the-sin-of Sodom, which-was-overthrown as-in-a-moment — and-no hands were-wrung over-her.

**7** And-the-poet lamented the-fall-of Zion's nobles and-the-horrors-of the-siege and-the-shame-of the-king.

**8** And-the-poet lamented the-fall-of Zion's nobles and-the-horrors-of the-siege and-the-shame-of the-king.

**9** And-the-poet lamented the-fall-of Zion's nobles and-the-horrors-of the-siege and-the-shame-of the-king.

**17** And-the-poet lamented the-fall-of Zion's nobles and-the-horrors-of the-siege and-the-shame-of the-king.

**18** And-the-poet lamented the-fall-of Zion's nobles and-the-horrors-of the-siege and-the-shame-of the-king.

**19** And-the-poet lamented the-fall-of Zion's nobles and-the-horrors-of the-siege and-the-shame-of the-king.

**20** And-the-poet lamented the-fall-of Zion's nobles and-the-horrors-of the-siege and-the-shame-of the-king.

**21** Rejoice and-be-glad, daughter-of Edom, dwelling in-the-land-of Uz; to-you also the-cup will-pass — you-will-become-drunk and-strip-yourself-bare.

**22** Your-iniquity is-completed, daughter-of Zion — He-will-not-again exile-you; He-will-punish your-iniquity, daughter-of Edom — He-will-uncover your-sins.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **4:1**: Ekhah yu'am zahav — 'How the gold is dimmed!' The fourth acrostic returns to the exclamation of chapter 1. Gold = the Temple vessels and the people themselves.

- **4:6**: Comparison with Sodom: Jerusalem's punishment exceeds Sodom's because it was prolonged. Sodom was overthrown 'in a moment' — Jerusalem's suffering was drawn out.

- **4:22**: Tam avonekh — 'Your iniquity is completed.' A glimmer of hope: punishment has a terminus. The suffering is not eternal.

— EMET
